gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI AC180's solar input is capped at 10 A (500W max, Voc 12-60 VDC), so the two 200 W panels in the AC180 + 2× 200 W kit only reach about 400 W if they are wired in series. Wired in parallel at roughly 20 V panel voltage, the 10 A cap holds them to about 200 W, and the second panel adds almost nothing in full sun.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited pages. StormWatts (stormwatts.com/articles/solar-generator-kits-compared-same-panel-watts, 2026-11-08) already explains series versus parallel against each station's amp limit for the Elite 200 V2 (12-60 V, 20 A), the DELTA 3 Max (13 A, Isc 18 A) and the Jackery 2000 v2 (400 W cap). It does not cover the AC180 or the single-panel ALLPOWERS SP037 kits. Our own page (dealectric.com/solar-generator-with-panels-included) lists the AC180 + 2× 200 W kit with no solar input spec. It applies the amp-band logic only to the Anker C1000 Gen 2 (8.2 A band, about 164 W). So the mechanism is partly known to rivals, but nobody has applied it to the AC180 kit or to the one-panel 400 W kits.
decides: This argues against the AC180 + 2× 200 W kit (link price $1,170.40, pre-order, dispatch Dec 14, 2026) for a shopper who will plug both panels in side by side. Its 400 W only appears with series wiring, and the kit is also a pre-order. It supports the single-panel ALLPOWERS kits that ship now: R2500 V2 + SP037 at $913.49 and S2000 Pro + SP037 at $917.93. There, one 400 W panel rated at 37.4 V goes into one XT60 input, so there is no series-or-parallel choice to get wrong. Among the 2× 200 W kits, the Elite 200 V2 (20 A per StormWatts) has the most room for parallel wiring of the BLUETTI options rivals cover. One pick-level fact for the writer: on the S2000 Pro + SP037 page, ALLPOWERS's own copy says the S2000 Pro takes '2* solar panel 200W in parallel (400W max)' and '650W max' with more panels. The kit's one 400 W panel is therefore already at the figure ALLPOWERS gives for a two-panel setup.

findings.label: Solar input limit
findings.source_title: BLUETTI AC180 Portable Power Station (BLUETTI EU)
findings.note: The page says verbatim: 'Solar Input: 500W Max., VOC 12-60VDC, 10A'. The US page (bluettipower.com/products/ac180) returned HTTP 429 twice. A search snippet of the US page showed the same '500W Max., VOC 12-60VDC, 10A', but I could not open it. The page gives no series or parallel guidance.

findings.label: Usable solar watts by wiring (arithmetic at the 10 A cap)
findings.value: about 200 W in parallel; up to about 400 W in series
findings.source_title: BLUETTI AC180 Portable Power Station (BLUETTI EU)
findings.note: This is arithmetic, not a test. Parallel: two 12 V-class 200 W panels run at about 20 V, so 10 A × ~20 V ≈ 200 W, about half of the 400 W of panels. Series: the panel voltages add, so about 10 A × ~40 V ≈ 400 W. StormWatts gives the SP200L at Voc 24.6 V and Isc 10.8 A, so two in series are about 49 V, which is under the 60 V ceiling. I could not confirm which BLUETTI 200 W panel model ships in the AC180 kit.

findings.label: Panel operating voltage
findings.note: The store text says verbatim: 'ALLPOWERS 400W solar panel provides 37.4V huge power for your solar generators'. Read with storecheck.py, which showed $379.05 and available. 400 W / 37.4 V ≈ 10.7 A at rated output, so one panel needs about 10.7 A at a single input.
